description: Complete for-loop forms and add break/continue/return control flow — C-style for, break with value, continue, inlined block bodies for correct return semantics, comprehensive e2e tests.

userStories.title: Compile break as control flow
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want break to exit the nearest enclosing for or while loop so that I can terminate iteration early.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser produces an AST_BREAK node (not AST_LIT_STRING) when encountering break
break with no argument exits the loop, loop expression evaluates to nil
break $value exits the loop, loop expression evaluates to $value
Compiler emits a jump instruction that targets the instruction after the loop
VM executes the jump correctly
break outside any loop is a compile-time error
break works in both for and while loops
Nested loops: break exits only the innermost loop
E2e test: for with early break produces correct output
E2e test: while with break produces correct output
E2e test: nested loop break exits only inner loop
E2e test: break $value returns the value from the loop expression
All existing tests still pass (no regressions)
userStories.notes: break is already lexed as TOKEN_BREAK but parsed as AST_LIT_STRING. Needs: new AST node type, compiler loop context stack for jump patching, new opcode or reuse of OP_JUMP. The compiler must track a stack of loop contexts so break knows where to jump. Use forward-jump patching (same technique as if/else). break $value requires leaving the value on the stack before jumping.

userStories.title: Compile continue as control flow
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want continue to skip to the next iteration of the nearest enclosing loop so that I can skip specific elements.
acceptanceCriteria: Parser produces an AST_CONTINUE node (not AST_LIT_STRING) when encountering continue
Compiler emits a jump instruction that targets the loop's increment/next-iteration point
VM executes the jump correctly
continue outside any loop is a compile-time error
continue works in both for and while loops
Nested loops: continue affects only the innermost loop
E2e test: for with continue skips correct elements
E2e test: while with continue skips to next iteration
E2e test: nested loop continue affects only inner loop
All existing tests still pass (no regressions)
userStories.notes: Same infrastructure as break (loop context stack, jump patching). continue jumps to the loop's continue point: for collection-based loops this is the next-element advancement, for while loops it's the condition re-check, for C-style for it's the step expression. Reuses the loop context stack from US-001.

userStories.title: Inline block-form for bodies (fix return semantics)
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want return inside a for block body to exit the enclosing proc, not just the loop body, matching the spec and while loop behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Block-form for $items { body } inlines the body into the enclosing function's bytecode (not wrapped in a closure)
Block-form for $items name { body } also inlines the body
return inside an inlined for-body exits the enclosing proc
return $value inside an inlined for-body returns the value from the enclosing proc
Lambda-form for $items [\\ body] remains closure-based — return exits the lambda
HOF-form for $items $callback remains closure-based — return exits the callback proc
Existing for-loop tests continue to pass (implicit $it, explicit binding, HOF, empty vec, upvalue capture)
E2e test: return from inside a for block exits the enclosing proc
E2e test: return $value from inside a for block returns the value from the proc
E2e test: return from lambda-form for only exits the lambda
All existing tests still pass (no regressions)
userStories.notes: Currently for block bodies are wrapped in closures and called via OP_EACH. Inlining means the compiler emits the iteration loop directly (like while): get collection length, loop counter, get element, bind as local ($it or named), compile body inline, increment counter, loop back. This is a significant compiler change — the for block forms switch from OP_EACH-based to direct loop emission. Lambda and HOF forms continue using OP_EACH unchanged. break/continue from US-001/US-002 must work with the inlined loop.

userStories.title: C-style for loop
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want to write C-style for loops with init, condition, and step expressions so that I can do counted/index-based iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: Syntax: for {init; cond; step} { body } where init, cond, step are separated by ;
Compiler distinguishes this form: first arg is a {} block with semicolons → C-style loop
Init expression runs once before the loop
Condition is checked before each iteration; loop exits when condition is falsy
Step expression runs after each iteration body
Loop variable declared in init is scoped to the loop (not visible after loop ends)
break works inside C-style for
continue skips to the step expression, then re-checks condition
return exits the enclosing proc
E2e test: basic counting for {mut i 0; ($i < 5); set i ($i + 1)} { print $i } → 0 1 2 3 4
E2e test: C-style for with break
E2e test: C-style for with continue
E2e test: nested C-style for loops
All existing tests still pass (no regressions)
userStories.notes: The parser needs to detect when for's first arg is a {} block — this distinguishes C-style from collection-based forms. The block contains three ;-separated sections. The compiler emits: init code, then loop (condition check → body → step → jump back). continue target is the step expression. break target is after the loop. Loop variable scoping: wrap in a begin/end scope so the init variable is not visible after the loop.

userStories.title: Comprehensive e2e test suite for all for forms
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a complete test suite covering all for forms and control flow interactions to prevent regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests in test/test_compiler.c (compile-and-run style checking stdout output)
Test: collection for + implicit $it (existing — verify still passes)
Test: collection for + explicit binding (existing — verify still passes)
Test: collection for + HOF callback (existing — verify still passes)
Test: for over empty collection (existing — verify still passes)
Test: upvalue capture in for body (existing — verify still passes)
Test: C-style for basic counting
Test: C-style for with break
Test: C-style for with continue
Test: C-style for nested
Test: break exits for loop (value is nil)
Test: break $value returns value from for expression
Test: break exits while loop
Test: break in nested loops exits only innermost
Test: continue in for skips element
Test: continue in while skips to next check
Test: continue in nested loops affects only innermost
Test: return from for block exits enclosing proc
Test: return from lambda-form for exits only the lambda
Test: break outside loop is compile error
Test: continue outside loop is compile error
All tests pass
userStories.notes: This story adds any tests not already covered by US-001 through US-004. It is the final verification sweep — ensures all combinations are tested and all existing tests still pass. Tests should be in test_compiler.c using the standard compile-and-run-check-stdout pattern.
